points.what: APAC orders fell 7.3% WoW, contributing -30 orders, the largest negative contribution among regions this week.
points.so_what: APAC's pullback was the main drag on total orders this week, more than offsetting gains elsewhere.

points.what: EMEA orders rose 27.6% WoW, contributing +43 orders, the largest positive contribution among regions.
points.so_what: EMEA's growth nearly offset the declines in APAC, North America, and LATAM, limiting the week's total order drop to just 0.6% WoW.

points.what: Facebook orders fell 28.1% WoW, contributing -16 orders, the largest negative contribution among traffic sources.
points.so_what: The Facebook pullback was a bigger drag on orders than any other traffic source's change this week.

points.what: AOV fell 3.2% WoW to $86.34, though it was still up 6.8% YoY.
points.so_what: The WoW decline in AOV, alongside the WoW drop in orders, is why revenue fell 2.9% WoW while orders fell only 0.6% WoW.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 0.7pp WoW to 13.8% and 1.5pp YoY.
points.so_what: The improving cancellation rate is a positive signal even in a week that missed the revenue target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of Apr 20 fell 1.1pp WoW to 10.3%, a notable change, but was up 0.4pp YoY.
points.so_what: The YoY increase means returns have not improved compared with last year despite the WoW easing.

points.what: New signups rose 8.0% WoW and 9.8% YoY to 257, while orders fell 0.6% WoW.
points.so_what: New customer growth accelerated even as order volume dipped slightly this week.
